["Section 1 of the order delegates about 50 separate presidential functions, each under its own statute (for example 5 U.S.C. 5514, 5702, 5742, 5911, 5942, 5942a and 5943; 7 U.S.C. 1011 and 1990; 10 U.S.C. 126, 1074 and 1085; 16 U.S.C. 831c and 831f; 20 U.S.C. 191 and 905; 22 U.S.C. 287e-1 and 2679). The packet holds the current text of none of these statutes and only two current-law records (the 3 U.S.C. 301 note and the 38 U.S.C. 111 note), so no paragraph other than those can be shown to rest on a statute still in force on 2026-10-14. Missing: the current text of each delegated statute, or a held current record for each paragraph.","Later instruments touching the order whose provisions the packet did not locate: Executive Order 11429 (September 9, 1968, cross-referenced), Executive Order 12107 (December 28, 1978) and Executive Order 12608 (September 9, 1987). Their provisions on Executive Order 11609 must be read and attached before any clause can be called unamended.","Paragraphs (22) and (23) of section 1 were revoked by Executive Order 12215 section 1-404 (May 27, 1980), which also revoked Executive Order 11713 that added them; section 4 was amended by Executive Order 11779 (April 19, 1974), subsection 7 by Executive Order 12466 (February 27, 1984) and Executive Order 12522 (June 24, 1985), and section 8 by Executive Order 12822 (November 16, 1992). A claim would need a per-paragraph state for every one of them with the before-and-after wording.","Inventory defects: the dossier has a duplicate-scope clause (sec1-b-dup2), no clause for section 7, and about 61 clauses whose spans were not checked against the original; a corrected inventory with new spans is required."]
